messages:
From: AuditOps Team <auditops@auditfirm.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG request — SDLC artifacts (code review, CI controls, secrets rotation)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the quick intake call this morning. As part of the SIG assessment for Northbridge Financial, we need an evidence bundle that demonstrates your secure SDLC controls for the past 12 months. At a minimum please include: 1) a code review extract showing reviewer IDs, PR ids, and approval timestamps for prod-deploying repos; 2) CI/CD credential rotation logs and the tagging of ephemeral tokens; 3) a change-approval chronology for emergency and normal releases over the last year; and 4) a short narrative (1 page) describing your gating policies (PR gating, mandatory reviewers, automated policy failures).

Delivery expectation: encrypted ZIP with a manifest by 2027-10-14 COB. If you have existing Drive links for extracts, that is fine but we prefer attachments when possible. If any item requires redaction, please include a short justification and a representative sample.

Please confirm receipt and estimated ETA.

Best,
Avery (AuditOps)
AuditOps | ThirdParty Audit

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Team — forwarding the request from AuditOps for Northbridge (attached). Can we assemble a package and a short gating narrative by COB 10/14?

Asks: 
- Marissa: can you pull a code-review extract (csv) for the repositories marked "prod" in the repo inventory? Need reviewer_id, PR id, timestamp, approvals, and a flag for whether an automated policy blocked merges.
- Jordan: can you export CI credential rotation traces (Vault/ephemeral token rotation logs) and a short note on rotation frequency + enforcement?
- Karthik: change-approval chronology — need records for emergency patches and normal releases, including who approved, timestamps, and rollback notes.

If any of these require redaction (PII or full diffs), call it out and provide a representative sample. I'll coordinate the ZIP and manifest.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Quick update: I exported the Vault rotation API traces for the period 2027-01-01 -> 2027-09-30. Files include service-account-token-rotation.csv and ephemeral-token-issue-trace.csv. Key points to call out in the narrative:
- All short-lived CI tokens are rotated on a 30-day cadence; ephemeral job tokens are TTL-limited to under 1 hour and are minted via OIDC flows.
- There are automated fail-open/lockdown policies in CI when a token issue is detected (see trace annotations).
- Redaction: I redacted full token ids and replaced with token-hash placeholders.

I uploaded the export to Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/s/SDLC-evidence/nbf-2027-10 (permission: view+comment for auditops@auditfirm.com).

Jordan Blake
Platform Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 14:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG request — SDLC artifacts (code review, CI controls, secrets rotation)

Attached the change-approval chronology and a short excerpt of emergency patch approvals. Highlights:
- Normal release approvals are performed via the Release Board (JIRA workflow) with at least 2 approvers: Release Manager + Service Owner.
- Emergency patches use the Emergency Approval flow (ticket tag: "emergency-release"); approvals are recorded in the ticket and follow-up postmortems are required within 48 hours.
- I am including an XLSX that maps ticket ids -> approver usernames -> approval timestamps -> rollback flag.

Attachments: change-approval-chronology.xlsx (contains columns: ticket, release_tag, approver, approval_ts, rollback_ts, notes).

Karthik Iyer
Director, Release Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hannah,

Received the bundle and the Drive link — thanks for the fast turnaround. We downloaded the sample CSVs and the change chronology and confirmed the following items are sufficient for our preliminary review: code-review extract with reviewer IDs, CI rotation traces (redacted), and the release approval chronology. A couple of small follow-ups: 1) can you provide an example policy rule that blocks merges (the policy id or the policy engine output for one blocked PR) so we can see the signal used to enforce gating? 2) For the emergency-release flow, include the postmortem ticket id for one recent patch (we saw the flag but need the follow-on details).

If you can drop those two items by 10/15 EOB we'll be able to advance to the next SIG questionnaire section.

Best,
Avery (AuditOps)
